slides.title: Construct A Hypothesis “If the “Checkout” is changed
slides.text: Construct A Hypothesis “If the “Checkout” is changed to “Complete My Order,” the conversion rates in the checkout will increase, because the copy is more specific and personalized.”

slides.title: Terminology • Response (or Dependent Variable, Outcome, Performance
slides.text: Terminology • Response (or Dependent Variable, Outcome, Performance metric) - a quantitative measure of the experiment’s objective • Factor (or Variable) - controllable variable that is thought to influence response. – Factors are assigned Values (or Levels, Versions). • Treatment (or Variant, Version) - a user experience being tested by assigning levels to the factors.

slides.title: A/B testing A/B testing is a way to
slides.text: A/B testing A/B testing is a way to compare two versions of a single variable typically by testing a subject’s response to variable A against variable B, and determining which of the two variables is more effective.

slides.title: A/B Testing • Pros: – Easy to set
slides.text: A/B Testing • Pros: – Easy to set up and interpret results – Plenty of free tools - cheap way to start testing – Lower traffic demands • Cons: – All-or-nothing approach (individual effects hard to assess if changing several things at a time)

slides.title: Multivariate Testing (MVT) • Multivariate testing is a
slides.text: Multivariate Testing (MVT) • Multivariate testing is a technique for testing a hypothesis in which multiple variables are modified. • The goal of multivariate testing is to determine which combination of variations performs the best out of all of the possible Combinations

slides.title: Multivariate Testing (MVT) • Pros: – Generates insights
slides.text: Multivariate Testing (MVT) • Pros: – Generates insights on interaction between multiple elements – Can substitute for A/B testing • Cons: – More involved to set up compared to A/B testing – Amount of visitor traffic required
